sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
U-shape:
```
33 c Y B B B B Y c c
34 c Y B B B B Y c c
35 c Y B B B B Y c c
36 c Y B Y Y B Y c c
37 B Y Y Y Y Y Y B B
```
So the U is: walls at columns 29 and 34 (rows 33–36), bottom at row 37 (columns 29–34), plus a 2px nub at row 36, columns 31–32 (Y Y). The nub is at the bottom-center of the interior. The piece's notch is 2px at the bottom-center (columns 31–32, row 16). So the piece fits on top of the nub: the piece's bottom row has a notch at columns 31–32, and the U's nub is at columns 31–32.
Piece:
```
13 Y Y Y Y
14 Y Y Y Y
15 Y Y Y Y
16 Y c c Y
```
To fit into the U, the piece's row 16 (Y c c Y) would sit on top of the U's row 36... the U's nub (columns 31–32) fills the piece's notch (columns 31–32). The piece's Y at columns 30, 33 of row 16 would sit on top of the U's walls? The U's walls are at columns 29, 34 — not 30, 33. Hmm, so the piece's bottom corners (30, 33) would be floating above the interior's B (columns 30, 33 of row 36 are B). Doesn't fully interlock, but visually the piece would be "inserted" into the U with the nub going into the notch.
So the goal is almost certainly: move the piece from (13–16, 30–33) to (33–36, 30–33) — i.e., drop it into the U. The piece needs to move down 20 rows.
How? The piece is 4 rows tall; the U's opening is at rows 33–36 (walls at columns 29, 34). The piece is at columns 30–33 — already horizontally aligned with the U's opening (interior columns 30–33). So the piece just needs to fall 20 rows.
What makes it fall? The bars! Maybe each bar controls a "gate" row? 10 bars... the piece needs to pass through rows 17–32 (16 rows). Hmm.
Or maybe the bars control gravity: when a specific bar is B, the piece falls one row per click?
Or maybe the piece falls when you click it, but only if the bars form a "path"? The piece is at columns 30–33. The bars are at columns 21, 26, 31, 36, 41. Bar 31 is directly below the piece (column 31 is within the piece's columns 30–33).
Wait — maybe the bars are "switches" and the piece falls one row per click on the piece, but the fall is blocked unless the bar below the piece's column is in the correct state. I clicked the piece at (14,31) when bar 31 was B/B (step 1), then B/w (step 6). Nothing happened.
Hmm, what if the piece doesn't fall — what if the U rises? Or the whole checkerboard scrolls?
Let me think about the ball again. Ball is at rows 51–59, columns 32–40 (center ~36). It's a 9x9 circle. Below the panel. Maybe the ball is a "ball of light" that you launch upward by clicking, and it travels up column 36... passing through the panel? The panel's bottom edge is at row 47. The bars are at rows 42–46. The ball would hit the bar at column 36 (bar 36). If bar 36 is "open" (w?), the ball passes through and... hits the piece? The piece is at columns 30–33, not 36. Hmm, no.
Or maybe the ball bounces off the bars like a pinball! The bars are "paddles" at rows 42–46. The ball is below the panel at rows 51–59. If the ball launches upward, it hits the panel's bottom edge (row 47) and... bounces?
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the layout: maybe the white panel is a "screen" and the ball is outside it. The game might be "aim the ball at the target": click to launch the ball from its position toward the click point? I clicked (55,20) — nothing. I clicked the ball (55,36) — nothing.
Hmm, what if you need to click the ball twice (first to select, second to launch)? Let me try: click the ball, then click the ball again. Or click the ball, then click the piece.
Actually — a new idea. What if the game is: the ball is the player, and it moves toward the clicked cell (like a "move to" cursor game)? I clicked (55,20) — the ball didn't move. So no.
Let me try a batch: click the ball twice, then observe.
